pages.title: Noren Curtains
pages.text: Noren are the split curtains that hang in doorways. Cut a block of wool on the stonecutter to get one in that color, or dye an existing noren instead: the dye changes the color and the pattern is kept. Four patterns exist — plain, striped, wavy and long — in all 16 wool colors.

pages.title: Plank Walls
pages.text: Plank walls come in every wood type, cut two at a time from the matching planks on the stonecutter — for the careful of purse.

pages.title: Tiles
pages.text: Tiles come in seven colors: cyan, orange, yellow, brown, blue, black and gray, made from deepslate tiles plus a dye. Every color has stairs, slabs and wall panels, and all of them can be made on the stonecutter.

pages.title: Paper Goods
pages.text: Two paper-made building blocks, each in a solid and a thin pane form. Both are cheap — sticks and paper — and both can be shaped into their variants on the stonecutter. They let light through rather than blocking it, so a room sealed with them stays bright, and they burn as fuel.

pages.title: Lanterns
pages.text: Four paper lanterns, red and white, plain or lettered, each bright enough on its own to light a whole room. A column of them reads as a single string. They have no recipe and are only found where structures generate.

pages.title: Wrought Iron Railings
pages.text: Blackened ironwork, which lends a room some gravity. It is stained from iron bars, and goes on to make pillars and candlesticks.
